# Itiha intelligence brief, 2026-11-22

**Tipu Sultan is today's top Wikipedia spike, at 2.31x his usual English readership, on the last day before the Tipu Short lapses. Record Guru Tegh Bahadur first, for tomorrow; Tipu goes up tonight only if both fit. The Indonesia long-form still brings 3.7 subscribers per 1,000 views against 2 for Asia, so Bali research starts.**

## This week: 3 decisions
1. **Script and publish a Short on Aurangzeb's order to execute Guru Tegh Bahadur, for 24 November.** (short, due 2026-11-24, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: Two days out, the top date on the radar, and it names Aurangzeb, the villain of the channel's two largest videos. Breakouts are the lever furthest behind: 0 subscribers from them this month against 1,692 planned. It rests on the date and the name: Mughal Shorts with no film behind them have landed below the usual.  
   First step: Script and record today. Open on Gurdwara Sis Ganj in Chandni Chowk, then Aurangzeb's order: an act of state, not a martyrdom story. Title starts “Guru Tegh Bahadur”. Publish 23 November, 17:00 IST.
2. **Script, record and publish one Tipu Sultan Short on the fall of Srirangapatna in 1799: who took the treasure, and who wrote his story afterwards.** (short, due 2026-11-20, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: Last day: it lapses by itself tomorrow. New today, Tipu Sultan is the top Wikipedia spike, his English readership at 2.31x its 30-day median, and on 21 November The Hindu reported his descendant asking for official celebrations and his textbook chapter back. The owner's own pick of 15 November. It comes second only because Tegh Bahadur's date cannot move.  
   First step: Only after Tegh Bahadur is recorded: if there is time left today, script, record and publish it tonight. If not, press Drop on the Today tab with a one-line note, so the list shows a choice, not a lapse.
3. **Script and publish a follow-up long-form for the Indonesia video's viewers: why Bali stayed Hindu when Java converted.** (long, due 2026-12-02, open since 2026-11-19)  
   Why: The test set for today is met: the Indonesia long-form brings 3.7 subscribers per 1,000 views against 2 for the Asia one, on 80,146 views and still climbing, and its comments are full of viewers from Java. Follow it while they still arrive. The Bali topic is a guess from those comments.  
   First step: After the Tegh Bahadur recording, start the source list: Majapahit's fall and the priests who moved to Bali. Put the Indonesia transcript in the scripts folder first, so the check shows where its viewers left.

Everything below is the evidence. Mark a decision done or dropped on the Brief tab; an open one stays here until then.

## Channel health
18,100 subscribers, up 800 in a week, against 100,000 by 28 September 2027. November's milestone is 20,212, which needs 74.2 net a day; the 7-day rate is 115.7. Projection basis: 28-day rate; the 7-day rate is a spike, so the week's jump is not carried forward: the month ends near 18,530, 1,682 short, and the channel is 1,474 behind the ramp today. Only 47.5% of net subscribers over 28 days came from videos; the rest is tied to no video and can stop without warning. The lever furthest behind is breakouts, 0 against 1,692 this month; one video of that size closes the month. Last week (16 to 22 November) two videos shipped and neither came from this list: the Indonesia long-form beat the usual for a long-form, and the Sonia Gandhi Short fell below the usual for a Short. What ships is the owner's own picks, so this week the list holds only the two dated Shorts and the Indonesia follow-up. Two standing numbers moved: long-form subscribers per 1,000 views over the 365-day window are down to 7.6, out of their usual range, and Chakla no longer carries the year's long-form reach: “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?” now holds 37.8% of long-form views over the 365-day window.

What's working
- “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” is the month's long-form: 80,146 views in 116 hours, 690 an hour, and one of three videos this month past the channel's top-hit line of 67 net subscribers. It brings more subscribers per view than the bigger Asia long-form: 3.7 per 1,000 views against 2.
- Long-form is still where subscribers come from: 82.0% of upload net subscribers over 28 days, and over the 365-day window one long-form view brings 7.81x the subscribers a Shorts view does.
- The best converter in the 90-day window is “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 13.3 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson fits both dated Shorts: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.” For Tipu, the document is the record of who shared his treasure; for Tegh Bahadur, the order itself.

What's wrong
- A week after both dated Shorts were set, neither has a script on disk, and last week none of the brief's picks shipped. Probable cause: the owner's own scripts fill the time (the Sonia Gandhi Short on 20 November, the Param Vir Chakra script written the same day, the ICS salaries Short reopened on 19 November). Test: none, it is a choice. Tegh Bahadur first, because its date will not move.
- The Sonia Gandhi Short is below the usual: 788 views in 48 hours (16.5 an hour) and 0 subscribers per 1,000 so far. Probable cause: Shorts on recent politics have landed below the usual here, and a book in the news did not change that, even with Rajiv Gandhi's English Wikipedia readership at 2.21x its median. Test: its day three, 23 November. If it stays low, keep recent-politics Shorts off the list for now.
- Long-form watch time fell 18.0% week over week while views fell only 5.0%: each view is shorter. The Indonesia long-form is watched for 26.2% of its length on average against 31.2% for Asia, and all three Ramayana long-forms lose most viewers in their first third. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing (211,193 long-form views over 28 days from Home and subscriptions against 5,923 from search; 41.5% of November's long-form views were engaged). Test: the Indonesia transcript in the scripts folder, so the check shows where viewers leave, before the Bali script is written.
- Shorts views fell 75.8% week over week to 2026-11-19: the Ravana film Shorts' run of 11 November has left the window, and the film Shorts after them stayed below the usual (“Every Ramayana Kept One Rule”, 1,728; the Constitution one, 1,404). Search brings only 30.5% of Shorts views over 28 days, out of its usual range. Probable cause: the film is in its third week and nothing dated has gone up since. Test: the Tegh Bahadur Short's day three, 26 November.

## Audience
Analytics runs to 2026-11-19, the Indonesia long-form's third day. Long-form is watched from the Home feed, Shorts from the Shorts feed, and most new subscribers click on the channel page rather than under a video.
- The channel page does more than any video: 1,023 subscribers over 28 days came with no video attached, against 716 net from all uploads. Community posts brought 2 on 416,471 views: they buy views, not subscribers.
- The Indonesia long-form reached Indonesia: Muslim viewers from Java say they grew up with the Ramayana, others correct the Majapahit detail, and Indian viewers say they subscribed. Nobody has given that audience a second video yet; Bali is it.
- Shorts live on the Shorts feed: 158,072 Shorts views over 28 days came from it, against 80,992 from search. A searched name at the front of the title still matters for the long tail, which is why both dated Shorts start with the person's name.

## How they are reacting
The Indonesia long-form still holds most of the week's comments: anger at the rewrite, viewers from Java answering, and a newer thread, people naming inculturation as a method of conversion, under both the Indonesia video and the Mother Mary Short.
- **Inculturation as a way to convert** (negative): "“Inculturation” - the strategy of appropriation, confuse and convert."
- **Anger at the rewrite** (negative): "So, Fanfiction trying to make themselves canon."
- **Viewers from Java** (positive): "I am a Muslim living in Java, Indonesia, and I have been familiar with the Ramayana and Mahabharata since childhood."
- **A correction on Majapahit** (mixed): "Rama were never worshiped in Classical Nusantara (present day countries describe as malay archipelago) esp. in the Majapahit era"
- **The Chola objection, still on top under the Asia video** (mixed): "“Never sent a single soldier…” ever heard of Chola Empire?"
- **The Sai Pallavi row** (negative): "Playing Maa Sita and saying that statement is contradictory. She didn't feel the pain of maa Sita when playing the role"

Requested topics
- Hindi versions of the long-forms (“aap hindi mee bhi video banao na”, under the Indonesia one)
- A Krishna video in the shape of the Asia Ramayana one
- Rajendra Chola's raid on Srivijaya, the top objection under the Asia long-form
- Bagan in Myanmar

## Competitors
The watchlist is still the Ramayana film and the boycott row around it. The two biggest outliers this month are Hindu Lifestyle Shorts that open by stating the claim they are about to knock down.
- **Hindu Lifestyle**: "Diwali is South Asian... wait.. what?"
  Why it worked: 160,938 views at 30.5x the channel's median, a Short. The first line is the claim in the other side's own words (“Diwali is not a Hindu festival. It's a South Asian festival.”), the second is one word, “What?”, and then the answer from what Hindus actually celebrate.
  Steal: The Tipu opening: say the line his admirers say about him, in their words, then turn straight to the record of who got rich from his death.
- **Hindu Lifestyle**: "Boycott the Ramayana? What?"
  Why it worked: 111,405 views at 21.1x the median: a parent speaking to other Hindu parents inside the boycott row, in the first person (“I took my eight and 5-year-old boys to see it”), with three reasons.
  Steal: Nothing this week. It is a voice in the row, not a history answer, and the channel's own film Shorts after 11 November fell below the usual. It does show the row still draws viewers, which is why the ban call below is marked skip rather than ignored.

Gaps
- Aurangzeb as a long-form: Mohak Mangal's “Reality of Aurangzeb” is still unanswered by every tracked channel and by Itiha. If the Tegh Bahadur Short lands, that is the long-form it points to.
- Japan's propaganda posters for India: The Emissary's Short (630,814 views) is the top competitor topic with no equivalent anywhere in Itiha's catalogue.

## Trending now, make this
- **today, short, 3/5**: Tipu Sultan: a Wikipedia spike on the Short's last day  
  Signal: English Wikipedia readership at 2.31x its 30-day median, 2,608 a day over three days. The Hindu (21 November): his descendant wants official celebrations and his textbook chapter restored. The Tipu Jayanti row has run in Marathi news since 19 November. (Wikipedia pageviews, news, decision)  
  Make: Publish tonight only if Tegh Bahadur is recorded first, titled with his name first: “Tipu Sultan's Death: Who Got Rich From It”. Otherwise press Drop.
- **today, short, 3/5**: Guru Tegh Bahadur, 24 November  
  Signal: The top date on the radar, two days out; the searched phrase is “guru tegh bahadur history”. The calendar flags the martyrdom framing as one to avoid. (Moments radar, calendar)  
  Make: Record today, publish 23 November at 17:00 IST, and judge it on 26 November and on search over the year, by the channel's own lesson: “Persecution memory with a named defender, released on its anniversary, earns search traffic for a year; judge it on lifetime search views, not on day-three feed widening.”
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: Winston Churchill's birth anniversary, 30 November  
  Signal: Eight days out. The radar's next step falls tomorrow: research with named sources and script a Short on the colonial mechanism, what the British record itself admits. (Moments radar)  
  Make: First claim on the slot Tipu frees: one Short on the Bengal famine of 1943, convicted from British papers (War Cabinet minutes, Leo Amery's diary), every quote checked before recording, published 30 November.
- **this_week, short, 1/5**: Two big films on 4 December: “Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace” and “Eetha”  
  Signal: Both are mass releases with trailers out (Salman Khan's war film, Shraddha Kapoor's biopic). The data does not say what either film is about. The radar's step is due now: find the subject and the three claims each film is likely to make. (Moments radar (Wikipedia release list))  
  Make: By 27 November, check what each film is about. If one is a real historical subject, it takes the slot Tegh Bahadur frees: a Short on what the film leaves out, for release day +1 to +9 (5 to 13 December), one person or one mystery, the villain in the first sentence. A mass release is how the channel's breakouts happened: Chhava gave three of four.
- **watch, skip, 2/5**: The VHP's call to ban the Ramayana film  
  Signal: In the news since 21 November (India Today, The Times of India), with Hindu Janajagruti Samiti threatening protests over Part 2. Hindu Lifestyle's boycott Short is at 21.1x its median. (News, competitors)  
  Make: Skip. The film is in its third week, the channel's last two film Shorts landed below the usual, and the headlines do not name the scene objected to, so there is nothing to check against the text.

## Topic ideas (voltage-checked)
- [4/5, long] **The Fake Veda Missionaries Wrote to Convert Hindus**  
  Empire mechanism: conversion run through a forged Hindu text, the same mechanism as the month's best long-form; Villain plus hypocrisy: missionaries writing a Veda (the Ezourvedam) to argue Hindus out of the Vedas; Religion and identity stakes: conversion; Hidden history: Voltaire took it for the oldest Veda; Francis Ellis showed in 1822 that missionaries had written it  
  source: Viewers named inculturation as a method of conversion under “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” and “Why Mother Mary Looks Different in Every Country You Visit”. A guess from those comments and the Indonesia video's result, not a test of this topic. Open on the day the book reached Voltaire and name who wrote it within the first half-minute. Check every date before scripting.

## Instagram (separate platform, separate audience)
Instagram has 25,546 followers, up 231 in 7 days, 33 a day. The Sonia Gandhi reel reached 3,678 with a 53.5% skip rate, worse than the level breakout reels stay under. Carousels remain the format that grows the account, at 3.7x the median reach of reels.

Do more
- Write carousels that correct the record (the revision lane)  
  50 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53.5 followers against 21.5 for the other lanes (40 posts). Median reach 15.9k vs 11.8k, conversion 3.77 vs 2.12 per 1k. 406 followers a month at stake.
- Build every carousel at 7-10 cards  
  The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 36 followers (90 posts); outside the band, 12 (15 posts). Pooled rate 2.97 vs 1.88 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact. 392 followers a month at stake.

Do less
- Stop making posts that get shared without bringing followers  
  17 of 103 rated posts are shared above the median (25.0/1k) but convert below it (2.1/1k): median 11.1k reach for a median 10 followers. The 35 posts that do both average 278 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen. 880 followers a month at stake.
- Stop posting single images  
  87 single images all time: 83.9k reach between them and 119 followers, 1.4 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 159.6. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken. 92 followers a month at stake.

## Housekeeping
- **now**: Put the Indonesia long-form's final script or transcript in the long-form scripts folder; the next refresh picks it up.  
  Its drop-off check still cannot run, and the Bali script starts this week. It should be written knowing where this one lost people.
- **this_week**: Upload the Malay Ramayana Short (Ravana getting his powers from Allah, on Instagram since 20 November) to YouTube on 25 or 26 November, title starting “Ravana”, with the Indonesia long-form as its related video.  
  The script is written and cut, and it was made to send viewers to the Indonesia long-form, which still averages 690 views an hour. Keep 23 November for Tegh Bahadur. That it sends viewers on is a guess.
- **this_week**: If not done yet, reply under the Majapahit correction on the Indonesia long-form (/replies drafts it).  
  It is among the most-liked comments on a video still climbing, and the Bali script will have to answer the same point. That a reply helps is a guess.
- **this_week**: If not done yet, check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” has only 12 views since 3 November.  
  A public Short gets at least a handful of views a day; almost none points to a visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.
